tools.name: create-document-index
tools.description:
Create a Pinecone document index: an index defined by a
schema of searchable "string" fields. Each field can declare "fullTextSearch"
(indexed for keyword search with BM25), "embed" (Pinecone embeds the text with a
hosted dense model for semantic search), "sparseEmbed" (a hosted sparse model),
or a combination. A good default is one field with both, for example
{"chunk_text": {"fullTextSearch": {"language": "en"}, "embed": {}}}, which
supports search by meaning and by exact terms on the same text. Fields you only
need to filter on are not declared here; send them as document metadata.
Use upsert-documents and search-document-index with the new index. This call blocks
until the index is ready. If an index with the same name already exists, it is
returned unchanged instead of erroring.

name.description: A unique name to identify the new index.

language.description: The language of the text, as an ISO 639-1 code such as "en". Defaults to "en".

stemming.description: Whether to stem terms. Defaults to false.

stopWords.description: Whether to remove stop words. Requires stemming. Defaults to false.

fullTextSearch.description: Index the field for full-text (BM25) search. Pass {} for the defaults.

model.description: A hosted dense embedding model. Defaults to "llama-text-embed-v2".

dimension.description: The vector dimension. Defaults to the model's default (1024).

embed.description:
Have Pinecone embed the field's text with a hosted dense model. Pass {} for
    the default model. An index can have at most one field with "embed".

model.description: A hosted sparse embedding model. Defaults to "pinecone-sparse-english-v0".

sparseEmbed.description:
Have Pinecone embed the field's text with a hosted sparse model. Pass {} for
    the default model. An index can have at most one field with "sparseEmbed".

fields.description: The searchable string fields of the index, keyed by field name.

cloud.description: The cloud provider for the index. Defaults to aws.

region.description: The region for the index. Common regions: aws (us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1), gcp (us-central1, europe-west1), azure (eastus, westeurope). Defaults to us-east-1.

tools.name: upsert-documents
tools.description:
Insert or update documents in a Pinecone document index
(one created with create-document-index). Each document needs an "_id" and
plain text in every field the index declares with "embed"; Pinecone embeds that
text on write, so never send vectors. Call describe-index first to see the
schema. Fields not in the schema are stored as metadata you can filter on.
Documents with an existing "_id" are replaced. Newly upserted records can take a few seconds
to be indexed and become visible to search results and index stats; if recent
data is missing, wait briefly and retry.

namespace.description: The namespace to upsert into. Defaults to "__default__".

additionalProperties.description: A field value. Must be a string, number, boolean, or array of strings.

items.description:
A document to upsert. Must have an "_id" field and plain text in each field
    the index declares with "embed".

documents.description: The documents to upsert. Larger sets are sent in batches of 96.

llm_provider.description: Optional. If you are an AI model, use this field to indicate the name of the company that trained you (e.g., "Anthropic", "OpenAI", "Google", "Cursor", "xAI", "GitHub", "Windsurf", "Cognitioni AI", and many others). tools.name: search-document-index
tools.description:
Search a Pinecone document index (one created with
create-document-index). Call describe-index first to see which fields declare
"embed", "sparseEmbed", or "fullTextSearch". Rank with one or more "scoreBy"
clauses:
- "embed": search by meaning on a field with "embed". Pass the query as plain
text; Pinecone embeds it with the field's model.
- "sparse_embed": search a field with "sparseEmbed" the same way.
- "text": keyword (BM25) search on one or more full-text fields. Good for exact
terms like IDs, error codes, and names.
- "query_string": Lucene-style query syntax. Don't pass "fields" (the API
rejects it); target fields with qualifiers inside the query, for example
'chunk_text:"exact phrase"', or omit qualifiers to search every full-text field.
An "embed" or "sparse_embed" clause must be the only clause; "text" and
"query_string" clauses can be combined. To rank by meaning and by exact terms,
run two separate searches: their scores are on different scales, so don't
compare them across searches. Returns matches with "_id", "_score", and the
fields named in "includeFields". Newly upserted records can take a few seconds
to be indexed and become visible to search results and index stats; if recent
data is missing, wait briefly and retry.

namespace.description: The namespace to search. Defaults to "__default__".

fields.description: The fields to score. "embed" and "sparse_embed" take exactly one; "text" takes one or more. Omit for "query_string", which rejects it.

scoreBy.description: The clauses that rank the documents.

topK.description: The number of matches to return. Defaults to 10.

filter.description:
An optional filter, such as {"category": {"$eq": "policy"}}. On a
      full-text field, "$match_phrase", "$match_all", and "$match_any" require
      terms, for example {"chunk_text": {"$match_all": "refund"}}.

includeFields.description: The fields to return with each match. Defaults to ["*"] (all stored fields).

llm_provider.description: Optional. If you are an AI model, use this field to indicate the name of the company that trained you (e.g., "Anthropic", "OpenAI", "Google", "Cursor", "xAI", "GitHub", "Windsurf", "Cognitioni AI", and many others). The exact formatting doesn't matter - approximate values are fine. tools.name: create-index-for-model
tools.description:
Create a Pinecone index with integrated inference, which
automatically embeds the text field named in "fieldMap". Supports AWS, GCP, and
Azure cloud providers. This call blocks until the index is ready to accept
upserts and queries, so no readiness polling is needed afterwards. If an index
with the same name already exists, it is returned unchanged instead of
erroring. For a new index, prefer create-document-index, which supports
full-text search and integrated embedding on the same field.

name.description: A unique name to identify the new index.

cloud.description: The cloud provider for the index. Defaults to aws.

region.description: The region for the index. Common regions: aws (us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1), gcp (us-central1, europe-west1), azure (eastus, westeurope). Defaults to us-east-1.

model.description:
Choose an embedding model:
          - "multilingual-e5-large" is an efficient dense embedding model
          trained on a mixture of multilingual datasets. It works well on messy
          data and short queries expected to return medium-length passages of
          text (1-2 paragraphs).
          - "llama-text-embed-v2" is a high-performance dense embedding model
          optimized for text retrieval and ranking tasks. It is trained on a
          diverse range of text corpora and provides strong performance on
          longer passages and structured documents.
          - "pinecone-sparse-english-v0" is a sparse embedding model for
          converting text to sparse vectors for keyword or hybrid search. The
          model directly estimates the lexical importance of tokens by
          leveraging their context.

text.description:
The name of the field in the data records that contains the text
            content to embed. Records in the index must contain this field.

fieldMap.description: Identify which field from your data records will be embedded.

embed.description: Configure an embedding model that converts text into a vector.

tools.name: upsert-records
tools.description:
Insert or update records in an integrated Pinecone index.
For a document index, use upsert-documents instead.
Text in the field named by the index's "fieldMap" is embedded automatically —
call describe-index first to confirm that field name. Records with an existing
"id" are overwritten. Newly upserted records can take a few seconds
to be indexed and become visible to search results and index stats; if recent
data is missing, wait briefly and retry.

additionalProperties.description: A field value. Must be a string, number, boolean, or array of strings.

items.description:
A record to upsert. Must have an "id" or "_id" field and contain text in
    the field specified by the index's "fieldMap".

records.description:

tools.name: search-records
tools.description:
Search an index for records that are semantically similar
to the query text. Only works with integrated-inference indexes (e.g. created
with create-index-for-model), which embed the query automatically; it fails on
standard indexes and document indexes (use search-document-index for those) — use
describe-index to check the index type. Returns hits
with "_id", "_score", and the record's stored "fields". Newly upserted records can take a few seconds
to be indexed and become visible to search results and index stats; if recent
data is missing, wait briefly and retry.

topK.description:
The number of results to return. 10 is a reasonable default; use a
      larger value (e.g. 50) when reranking, so the reranker has more
      candidates to choose from. Very large values increase latency and
      response size.

filter.description:
A filter can be used to narrow down results. Use the syntax of
        MongoDB's query and projection operators: $eq, $ne, $gt, $gte, $lt,
        $lte, $in, $nin, $exists, $and, $or. Make sure the records in the index
        contain the fields that you are filtering on. To discover which fields
        exist, run a search without a filter and inspect the "fields" of the
        returned hits. Filtering on a field that records do not contain
        returns no results.

query.description: A query to search for records.

rerank.description:
Reranking can help determine which of the returned records are most
  relevant. When reranking, use a "query" with a "topK" that returns more
  results than you need; then use "rerank" to select the most relevant
  "topN" results.

model.description:
Choose a reranking model:
- "cohere-rerank-3.5" is Cohere's leading reranking model, balancing performance
and latency for a wide range of enterprise search applications.
- "bge-reranker-v2-m3" is a high-performance, multilingual reranking model that
works well on messy data and short queries expected to return medium-length
passages of text (1-2 paragraphs).
- "pinecone-rerank-v0" is a state of the art reranking model that out-performs
competitors on widely accepted benchmarks. It can handle chunks up to 512 tokens
(1-2 paragraphs).

topN.description:
The number of results to return after reranking. Must be less than or
      equal to the value of "query.topK".

rankFields.description:
The fields to rerank on. This should include the field name specified
    in the index's "fieldMap". The "bge-reranker-v2-m3" and
    "pinecone-rerank-v0" models support only a single rerank field.
    "cohere-rerank-3.5" supports multiple rerank fields.

query.description:
An optional query to rerank documents against. If not specified, the
      same query will be used for both the initial search and the reranking.

instructions:
Pinecone is a vector database that provides AI
tools and applications with fast, scalable, and flexible vector search.

Instructions for usage:
- Always search the documentation before attempting to explain or write code for
Pinecone. When writing code, always refer to examples from the documentation. Do
not make assumptions about usage. Always use the latest SDK version.

- If the code uses an index or namespace, make sure you use the correct names I
have configured or help me create new ones.

- Always use a consistent schema for records in an index. Do not use different
field names in the same index. Always put the text content in the field named in
the index's "fieldMap". Do not use objects as field values. Do not include a
"metadata" field.

- When searching for records, make sure to use a query that accurately reflects
my needs. Only use a filter if you are sure it will help me find the records I
need. Craft filters knowing the schema of the data in the index.

- If you receive an error, read the error response to understand what went
wrong. "MCP error -32602" means your input was wrong. Correct your input by
following the instructions carefully.
